{"tool":"datasheet","tag":"FV-106-2","question":"Which seal or piston ring materials are available, and what temperatures are they good for?"}

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [20, 21, 7, 15, 12, 14, 13, 18]:
The datasheet lists several plug-seal materials, with temperature limits depending on the seal design and service. It also lists UHMWPE for the Class VI seal ring. [pp. 7, 20]

- **Two-piece valve plug seal** (standard for NPS 1–6 valves except those with a Cavitrol III cage): carbon-filled PTFE, **−73 to 232 °C** (−100 to 450 °F); ethylene-propylene, **−40 to 232 °C** (−40 to 450 °F); fluorocarbon, **−18 to 204 °C** (0 to 400 °F); or nitrile, **−40 to 71 °C** (−40 to 160 °F) for air and hydrocarbons, or **−40 to 82 °C** (−40 to 180 °F) for other compatible fluids. The datasheet says fluorocarbon is not for steam or ammonia and is not recommended for water above 82 °C (180 °F); nitrile cannot be used with fire-resistant hydraulic oils. [p. 20]
- **Spring-loaded valve plug seal:** PTFE with an N10276 spring, **−73 to 232 °C** (−100 to 450 °F); or PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring, **−73 to 316 °C** (−100 to 600 °F). For the latter, the maximum is **260 °C (500 °F) in oxidizing service**. These spring-loaded seal options are standard on NPS 8 valves and NPS 1–6 valves with Cavitrol III cages, and optional on NPS 1–6 valves with other cages. [pp. 20–21]
- **Class VI seal ring:** UHMWPE (ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene), with a listed trim temperature limit of **−29 to 66 °C** (−20 to 150 °F) for the 17-4 stainless-steel cage options. With the 316 stainless-steel/ENC cage options, the limit is **−198 to 66 °C** (−325 to 150 °F). [p. 7]

For the PTFE/graphite spring-loaded seal, use of PEEK anti-extrusion rings is specified; PEEK means polyetheretherketone. The datasheet also lists PEEK anti-extrusion rings themselves as “not limiting factors.” [p. 20]

The datasheet lists these seal options: carbon-filled PTFE (−73 to 232 °C); ethylene-propylene (−40 to 232 °C); fluorocarbon (−18 to 204 °C); nitrile (−40 to 71 °C for air and hydrocarbons, or −40 to 82 °C for other compatible fluids); spring-loaded PTFE (−73 to 232 °C); and spring-loaded PTFE/graphite (−73 to 316 °C, limited to 260 °C in oxidizing service).
